Characteristics - SPECIFIC LEARNING DISABILITIES
Characteristics of Specific Learning Disabilities
The characteristics of specific learning disabilities are as unique as the learners themselves. No two people with a specific learning disability presents exactly the same. Some of the characteristics are typical of all learners. However, people with specific learning disabilities display multiple symptoms and do not outgrow them over time. Below are common characteristics of all learning disabilities. Examples of the characteristics are found in the parenthesis.
Common Characteristics:
Short attention span (has trouble focusing on one task for a long period of time)
Poor memory (Often has to ask for repetition of directions/steps, might not remember something previously learned)
Difficulty following directions especially when they contain one or more steps (ex. long-division)
Inability to discriminate between/among letters, numerals, or sounds (Switching b for d, 5 for S, etc.)
Poor reading and/or writing ability (at least one grade level below their peers)
Poor executive functioning skills (often loses papers, difficulty keeping track of long-term projects)
Sensory needs (need to move while working)
Sometimes Displayed:
Different performance from day to day
Letters in incorrect sequence
They says one thing, but mean another
Has trouble with change
Difficulty listening and remembering
Difficulty knowing right from left
Difficulty telling time
Difficulty sounding out words
Reverses letters when writing
Inappropriate responses
Difficulty obtaining vocabulary and concepts
Delayed/immature speech development
